title: Pocket Prefill Orchestration: budget-aware prefill coordinator and quantization hygiene
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds a tenant-scoped prefill coordinator (pocket prefill) to enforce small budgeted warmups + a quantization hygiene validator that gates risky quant profiles. Improves unit economics for low-traffic tenants and prevents quant regressions. Backwards-compatible config flags, no DB migrations.
description:
Context: small tenants and bursty traffic patterns were causing expensive cold-starts and over-provisioning. This PR implements a 'pocket prefill' coordinator (tenant-scoped, budget-limited warmups) and a lightweight quantization hygiene checker that runs during model rollout to avoid accuracy-driven cost regressions. Motivation: reduce per-tenant unit cost without impacting SLAs; provide safe defaults for prefill size and quant profiles and an opt-in audit step for new quant packs. Checklist: - [x] Implement pocket prefill coordinator and per-tenant budget configs - [x] Integrate telemetry + cost attribution hooks - [x] Add quant hygiene validator and simple heuristics (perplexity / sample-regression thresholds) - [x] E2E test for low-traffic warmup path - [x] Docs and helm values entry. Behavioral summary: a new coordinator service watches incoming tenant traffic and applies a tiny warmup window (< 100 tokens aggregated, default 20 tokens) when a cold-model request for a tenant is observed. The coordinator consults tenant budget caps and global emergency overrides. Prefill decisions are logged to prefills.metrics and attributed to tenant_id for unit economics reporting. The quant hygiene validator runs as part of model rollout in the model-registry pipeline; it runs a lightweight eval on a small canonical sample set and rejects quant packs if quality drop > configured delta (default 2.5% relative). Example config (helm values snippet):
prefill:
  enabled: true
  pocketDefaultTokens: 20
  pocketMaxTokensPerHour: 1000
quantHygiene:
  enabled: true
  maxRelativeDropPct: 2.5
Commits: 3 commits - 1) pocket prefill coordinator and API surface; 2) telemetry hooks, metrics and cost attribution; 3) quant-validator, tests and docs. Files changed (high level): services/prefill/controller.go (coordinator logic), pkg/econ/prefill_budgeter.py (budget enforcement), integrations/quant-validator/validator.py (hygiene heuristics), telemetry/prefill_metrics.yaml (metric exports), helm/prefill/values.yaml (defaults and toggles), tests/e2e/prefill_budget_test.py (integration), docs/operational/pocket-prefill.md (runbook). Testing / CI: full build and unit tests passed; e2e prefill path ran in ephemeral cluster (integration job) and passed against synthetic low-traffic scenario. Performance: median added latency for non-prefill requests unchanged; prefill path adds ~6ms CPU overhead per decision (measured in bench) and reduces average cold-start token cost by ~18% for the tested tenant cohort. Review conversation (summary): - Aisha: asked for clearer backoff semantics when prefill fails; requested additional test for race between concurrent first-requests. Author reply: implemented backoff (exponential with jitter) and added test. - Diego: requested the quant validator be tolerant of tenant-specific gold sets; added per-tenant override charts and documented fallback plan. - Noah: nit on logging verbosity; reduced DEBUG noise and added structured fields for tenant_id and request_id. CI notes: initial CI run showed a flaky e2e related to synthetic cluster teardown; reran and passed. Merge: squash and merge after approvals. Merge method: squash
